scope: Read-only review of model source, finite-state checker, exact negative controls, saved traces, guide, examples, transition ownership map and pinned D04/D05/D06/D09/D12 contracts. No implementation edits.
review_conclusions: The checker explores all candidate reachable states, preserves a shortest BFS safety counterexample, treats resource exhaustion and non-goal cycles as inconclusive, and does not replace liveness with existence of one successful schedule. Its universal progress fixed point matched the independent DFS oracle in all 4096 small graphs.

Finite-progress assumptions are explicit. The model does not silently assume fairness to escape a cycle. The documented progress result applies to the finite atomic-transition models, not arbitrary runtime schedules or unbounded actors.
Logical admission and physical owner lifetime are distinct. Atomic Open/AddRef is preserved; split admission and missing rollback controls demonstrate post-close admission and leaked leases.

Retirement separates setup/start return, native quiet, cancellation registration drain and control-call drain. Pre-entry, synchronous cancellation, callback-before-start-return, rejection and retained quarantine states are covered. Omitting each leg has its own actual violation, and registration omission is correctly described as premature cleanup success rather than invented use-after-free.

Result models preserve native terminal authority, cancellation-request separation, sole take ownership transfer, result lifetime after operation release, callback reference release, and conversion failure disposal. Negative controls target terminal rewrite, double transfer and premature release.

Dispatcher close discards queued work and joins active handlers separately from native retirement; timeout affects only the caller wait, and self-wait is rejected. The missing-handler-drain control demonstrates early cleanup success.

The one-slot mailbox model preserves atomic dirty/scheduled recheck and coalesces only idempotent cleanup state. Separate stale read/unschedule mutation reproduces a real lost wake without periodic polling masking it.

All reported candidate counts are tied to verified committed source and raw artifacts. Only the smallest real mailbox graph was independently re-enumerated; this review does not misrepresent the author full-suite run as a second independent execution.

Documentation and evidence state the absence of weak-memory, arbitrary CLR/Rust/FFI, intermodel composition, unbounded liveness, Native AOT, real-domain or performance proof. Future refinement remains explicitly not_yet_bound to A03/A06/A07/A08, which is the proper A19 boundary.
limitations: No claim of full-platform acceptance or production-algorithm equivalence.
No replay of the complete author model suite was necessary after the focused independent oracle/provenance checks.
